# districtry

> Click a point, or type an address, and see every civic district that covers it — and who holds those seats. 50 instances across Illinois, New York, California, Wisconsin, Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota, Kentucky, Indiana, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi, Louisiana, Missouri, Virginia, West Virginia, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Nevada, Arizona, New Jersey, New Hampshire, Texas, Florida, Ohio, Washington, Massachusetts, Colorado, Maryland, Alabama, Oregon, Connecticut, Utah, Kansas, New Mexico, Nebraska, Idaho, Hawaii, Maine, Montana, Rhode Island, Delaware, South Dakota, North Dakota, Alaska, Vermont and Wyoming. Every boundary and every name comes from a published source and is cited to it.

Free, no account, no tracking of individuals. The map runs in the browser; what each page sends to whom is listed at https://districtry.com/privacy.html.

## The whole site

- [districtry](https://districtry.com/): the front door. Type an address and it opens whichever instance covers it, with the point already selected; a point nobody covers is told so rather than routed somewhere wrong.
- [Privacy](https://districtry.com/privacy.html)
- [Sponsorship](https://districtry.com/sponsorship.html)
- [Traffic report](https://districtry.com/traffic.html)
- [About districtry](https://districtry.com/about.html)
- [How districtry uses AI](https://districtry.com/ai.html)
- [Report a problem or leave a comment](https://districtry.com/feedback.html)
- [How to use districtry](https://districtry.com/help.html)

## Illinois

97 counties. Wards, county boards, police districts and beats, school zones, judicial subcircuits, and the people who hold those seats.

- [Illinois district lookup](https://districtry.com/il/): 42 layers, 97 counties.
- [Chicago 2027 candidates by ward](https://districtry.com/il/chicago-candidates.html)
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/il/congress.html)
- [Who is my county commissioner?](https://districtry.com/il/county-board.html): links a page per county, 100 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [2026 precinct election results](https://districtry.com/il/election-results.html)
- [Who runs my fire protection district?](https://districtry.com/il/fire-district.html)
- [What judicial subcircuit am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/judicial-subcircuit.html)

## California

All 58 counties: cities and towns, unified, elementary and high school districts, ZIP codes and the nearest post office, plus the California Senate, Assembly and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. San Francisco in full: its supervisor districts and precincts, neighborhoods, police districts and stations, fire stations, school attendance areas and sites, libraries and voting centers, and the BART board, which also covers Alameda and Contra Costa counties. Tribal lands are not drawn yet, and county, city and school board officials outside San Francisco are not named yet; the Data gaps panel says why.

- [California district lookup](https://districtry.com/ca/): 22 layers, statewide, San Francisco in depth.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ca/congress.html)
- [2026 precinct election results](https://districtry.com/ca/election-results.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ca/sources.html)
- [Who is my CA state legislator?](https://districtry.com/ca/state-legislature.html)
- [What supervisor district am I in?](https://districtry.com/ca/supervisor-district.html)
- [California district questions](https://districtry.com/ca/faq.html)

## Michigan

All 83 counties: commissioner districts, compiled by the state from the plan each county's apportionment commission files — plus townships and charter townships, cities and villages, school districts and intermediate school districts, circuit courts and Court of Appeals districts, and the Michigan Senate, House and U.S. House seats, and who holds those.

- [Michigan district lookup](https://districtry.com/mi/): 19 layers, all 83 counties.

## Minnesota

All 87 counties and their county commissioner districts: judicial and watershed districts, townships and cities, voting precincts, school districts and school board districts, ZIP codes, tribal land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Minnesota Senate, House and U.S. House districts, and who holds the U.S. House seats. County commissioners, school board members and the councils of the cities over 25,000 people are named for the winner of each seat's most recent election in the Secretary of State's results, and a tribal council is named where the nation publishes its own list. Nobody is named yet on the judges' benches, the two state chambers or the smaller cities' councils, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Minnesota district lookup](https://districtry.com/mn/): 22 layers, all 87 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/mn/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/mn/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 87 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [2026 precinct election results](https://districtry.com/mn/election-results.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/mn/sources.html)

## Kentucky

All 120 counties: each county's fiscal court, elected officers and conservation district board, cities with their mayors and councils, voting precincts and census county divisions, school districts, the school board divisions of Jefferson and Rowan counties, and the Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, circuit court and district court districts — plus the Kentucky Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for each U.S. House seat. County and city officials are named from the Department for Local Government's directories, conservation district boards from the Division of Conservation's sheets, and judges from the Court of Justice's own pages. Nobody is named yet on the two state chambers or the school boards, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Kentucky district lookup](https://districtry.com/ky/): 16 layers, all 120 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ky/congress.html)
- [Who runs my county?](https://districtry.com/ky/county-government.html): links a page per county, 120 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ky/sources.html)
- [Kentucky district questions](https://districtry.com/ky/faq.html)

## Indiana

All 92 counties: each county's commissioners and county council, townships, cities and towns, voting precincts, school districts, the Indianapolis Public Schools board districts, conservancy districts, ZIP codes, the Pokagon Band's trust land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Court of Appeals districts whose voters decide whether its judges stay, and the Indiana Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for each U.S. House seat. County officials, township trustees and boards, and the mayors and councils of most places over 25,000 people are named for the winner of each seat's most recent election in the Election Division's certified results; three towns' councils and the Pokagon Band's council are named from their own pages, conservancy district boards from the Department of Natural Resources' directory, and the county council districts are drawn in 55 counties. Nobody is named yet on the two state chambers, the Court of Appeals, the school boards or the smaller towns' councils, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Indiana district lookup](https://districtry.com/in/): 18 layers, all 92 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/in/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/in/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 92 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/in/sources.html)
- [Indiana district questions](https://districtry.com/in/faq.html)

## North Carolina

All 100 counties: each county's board of commissioners, townships, cities and towns, city council districts, voting precincts, school districts and school board districts, ZIP codes, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians' land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the North Carolina Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for every seat. County commissioners are named for the winner of each seat's most recent election in the State Board of Elections' results, the mayor and council of each of the 42 cities and towns above 25,000 people from each place's own pages or, for two, the State Board's results, and each county's conservation district board from the Soil and Water Conservation Commission's directory. Nobody is named yet on the councils of smaller cities and towns, the school boards or the Eastern Band's council, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [North Carolina district lookup](https://districtry.com/nc/): 18 layers, all 100 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/nc/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/nc/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 100 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [2026 precinct election results](https://districtry.com/nc/election-results.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/nc/sources.html)
- [Who is my NC legislator?](https://districtry.com/nc/state-legislature.html)
- [District questions](https://districtry.com/nc/faq.html)

## Oklahoma

All 77 counties and their commissioner districts: cities and towns, city council wards, census county divisions, school districts, conservation districts, ZIP codes, the tribal areas the Census draws, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the district court judicial districts and the Oklahoma Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with a member named for every U.S. House seat and nearly every legislative one. Each county's three commissioners are named from the State Election Board's roster, and the mayor and council of each of the 16 cities above 25,000 people from each city's own pages or, for Muskogee, its official election results and news reports. Each conservation district's office, telephone and e-mail come from the Conservation Commission's directory. Nobody is named yet on the councils of smaller cities and towns, the school boards, the district courts or the conservation district boards, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Oklahoma district lookup](https://districtry.com/ok/): 17 layers, all 77 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ok/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/ok/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 77 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ok/sources.html)
- [Who is my Oklahoma legislator?](https://districtry.com/ok/state-legislature.html)
- [District questions](https://districtry.com/ok/faq.html)

## South Carolina

All 46 counties and their county council districts: cities and towns, city council districts, voting precincts and census county divisions, school districts and school board districts, ZIP codes, the Catawba Nation's land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the South Carolina Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for every seat, and the judicial circuits. Each council seat names the winner of its most recent election in the State Election Commission's certified results. The mayor and council of each of the 17 cities and towns above 25,000 people are named from the place's own pages, and each county's conservation district board from the Department of Natural Resources' pages. Nobody is named yet on the councils of smaller cities and towns, school boards or circuit courts, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [South Carolina district lookup](https://districtry.com/sc/): 17 layers, all 46 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/sc/congress.html)
- [Who is on my county council?](https://districtry.com/sc/county-council.html): links a page per county, 46 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/sc/sources.html)
- [Who is my SC legislator?](https://districtry.com/sc/state-legislature.html)
- [District questions](https://districtry.com/sc/faq.html)

## Tennessee

All 95 counties and their county commission districts: civil districts, cities and towns, city council districts, voting precincts, school districts and school board districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Tennessee Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat, and the judicial districts. County commissioners are named from each county's own pages where the county publishes a current list, and the mayor and council of each of the 28 cities and towns above 25,000 people from the city's own pages. Nobody is named yet on the councils of smaller cities and towns, school boards or judicial districts, and the Data gaps panel lists what is missing and why.

- [Tennessee district lookup](https://districtry.com/tn/): 19 layers, all 95 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/tn/congress.html)
- [County commission district lookup](https://districtry.com/tn/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 61 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/tn/sources.html)
- [Who is my Tennessee legislator?](https://districtry.com/tn/state-legislature.html)
- [Tennessee district questions](https://districtry.com/tn/faq.html)

## Arkansas

All 75 counties and their quorum court districts: townships, cities and towns, city council wards, voting precincts, school districts and school board zones, fire districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Arkansas Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat, and the Court of Appeals districts and judicial circuits. Every county judge is named, and so is the justice of the peace for nearly every district, from the county's own site where it numbers its justices and otherwise from the 2024 election results while the winner is still on the Association of Arkansas Counties' list. The mayor and council of each of the 19 cities above 25,000 people are named from the city's own pages. Nobody is named yet on the councils of smaller cities and towns, school boards, fire districts or courts, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Arkansas district lookup](https://districtry.com/ar/): 18 layers, all 75 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ar/congress.html)
- [Who is on my quorum court?](https://districtry.com/ar/quorum-court.html): links a page per county, 75 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ar/sources.html)
- [Who is my Arkansas legislator?](https://districtry.com/ar/state-legislature.html)
- [Arkansas district questions](https://districtry.com/ar/faq.html)

## Mississippi

All 82 counties and their boards of supervisors: cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians' land, the Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, chancery and circuit court districts, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Mississippi Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. Every county's five supervisors and five election commissioners are named from the Secretary of State's directory, and the court districts' judges from the Judiciary's own lists. Supervisor district lines are drawn in the 23 counties whose current map is confirmed, and the Data gaps panel says why the other 59 are not.

- [Mississippi district lookup](https://districtry.com/ms/): 17 layers, all 82 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ms/congress.html)
- [Who is my county supervisor?](https://districtry.com/ms/county-supervisor.html): links a page per county, 82 of them, each naming every member with the board of supervisors' office address and telephone where the Secretary of State's directory prints them.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ms/sources.html)
- [Who is my Mississippi legislator?](https://districtry.com/ms/state-legislature.html)
- [Mississippi district questions](https://districtry.com/ms/faq.html)

## Louisiana

All 64 parishes and their police juries and councils: cities, towns and villages, voting precincts, school districts, ZIP codes, the land of Louisiana's four federally recognized tribes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Louisiana Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. Every parish's police jury or council and its president where it elects one, the mayors and councils of 302 cities, towns and villages, and the members of all 69 school boards are named from the Secretary of State's list of elected officials. Parish district lines are drawn in the 6 parishes whose current map is confirmed, and the Data gaps panel says why the other 58 are not.

- [Louisiana district lookup](https://districtry.com/la/): 17 layers, all 64 parishes.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/la/congress.html)
- [Who runs my parish?](https://districtry.com/la/parish-government.html): links a page per parish, 64 of them, each naming every member with the telephone the Secretary of State's list prints for a member where it prints one, and the body's office address where three or more members give the same one.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/la/sources.html)
- [Who is my Louisiana legislator?](https://districtry.com/la/state-legislature.html)
- [Louisiana district questions](https://districtry.com/la/faq.html)

## Missouri

All 114 counties and the City of St. Louis: cities, towns and villages, townships, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Missouri Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. Every county's commission, council or legislature and its elected officers are named from the Secretary of State's Missouri Roster, and three charter councils from the counties' own websites. County commission district lines are drawn in the 30 counties whose map has been found or sent, and the map shades the other 84 until theirs are.

- [Missouri district lookup](https://districtry.com/mo/): 13 layers, 38 counties in depth.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/mo/congress.html)
- [Who runs my county?](https://districtry.com/mo/county-government.html): links a page per county, 114 of them, each naming every member with the telephone and e-mail the Secretary of State's Missouri Roster, or a charter county's own website, prints beside each member.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/mo/sources.html)
- [Who is my Missouri legislator?](https://districtry.com/mo/state-legislature.html)
- [Missouri district questions](https://districtry.com/mo/faq.html)

## Virginia

All 95 counties and 38 independent cities: each county's board and each city's council and the districts they are elected from, magisterial districts, cities and towns, voting precincts, school divisions and school board districts, ZIP codes, the land of the Pamunkey, Mattaponi and Rappahannock tribes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Virginia Senate, House of Delegates and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. Board, council, school board and soil and water conservation members are named from the Department of Elections' results, as are 165 of the 189 towns' mayors and 88 of their councils, a few of them from the town's own page. The Data gaps panel says which seats are not named and why.

- [Virginia district lookup](https://districtry.com/va/): 17 layers, all 133 counties and cities.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/va/congress.html)
- [2026 precinct election results](https://districtry.com/va/election-results.html)
- [Who runs my county or city?](https://districtry.com/va/local-government.html): links a page per county or city, 127 of them, each naming every member with the election, or the county's or city's own page, that names each one, and no contact details yet.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/va/sources.html)
- [Who is my Virginia legislator?](https://districtry.com/va/state-legislature.html)
- [Virginia district questions](https://districtry.com/va/faq.html)

## West Virginia

All 55 counties: each county's commission and elected officers, magisterial districts, cities, towns and villages, school districts, ZIP codes, Charleston's 20 council wards and the members elected from them, and the nearest police station, fire and EMS station and post office — plus the West Virginia Senate, House of Delegates and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. County commissioners and officers are named from the Secretary of State's directory of county officials, and legislators from the Legislature's own rosters. School board members, judges and the other cities' councils are not named yet, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [West Virginia district lookup](https://districtry.com/wv/): 12 layers, all 55 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/wv/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/wv/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 55 of them, each naming every member with the telephone and e-mail the Secretary of State's directory prints beside each commissioner, and the commission's office.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/wv/sources.html)
- [Who is my WV legislator?](https://districtry.com/wv/state-legislature.html)
- [West Virginia district questions](https://districtry.com/wv/faq.html)

## Georgia

All 159 counties: county commission and school board districts where the county's own elections confirm the map, voting precincts, judicial circuits with their judges and district attorneys, cities and towns, census county divisions, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Georgia Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. County commissioners and school board members are named from the Secretary of State's election results where an election since November 2024 chose them. The Data gaps panel says which seats are not named and why.

- [Georgia district lookup](https://districtry.com/ga/): 15 layers, all 159 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ga/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/ga/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 152 of them, each naming every member with the election on the Secretary of State's results site that named each one, and no contact details yet.

- [Who is my Georgia legislator?](https://districtry.com/ga/state-legislature.html)

## Arizona

All 15 counties: cities and towns, unified, elementary and high school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus Arizona's 30 legislative districts, each electing one senator and two representatives, and its U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. Tribal lands are not drawn yet, and county, city and school board officials are not named yet; the Data gaps panel says why.

## Where the answers come from

Each instance's sources page carries one row per layer: what it answers, the publisher its boundary comes from, where the names on its card come from, and the ground it answers on. That page is generated from the same list that registers the layers, so a layer cannot ship without a row.

Officeholder names are never guessed. Where no verifiable roster exists, a card links the official body instead of inventing a name, and what the project does not know is recorded rather than left blank — each instance ships a machine-readable list of its own gaps at `<instance>/data/app/coverage-gaps.json`.

Sources last reverified between November 10, 2026 and September 29, 2026, per instance.

This is a civic reference tool and it disclaims legal precision. Confirm a district assignment with the government office that draws it before relying on it for anything official.

## Terms

`https://districtry.com/robots.txt` publishes a Content-Signal, and these are the values in it: ai-input=yes, ai-train=no, search=yes, use=reference.

In plain words: indexing and search are welcome, and so is grounding an answer in these pages, on the terms the signal names — by reference, with a link back to the page that names the person, so a reader can check the government source behind it. Training is reserved. No crawler is disallowed by name: a site that wants its answers found does not gain anything by refusing the clients that find them.

The boundaries and rosters are public records from the publishers each sources page names; this project's own work is the collection, the citation and the code.

Corrections: corrections@overberg.co. Source: https://github.com/ThursdaysFamous/districtry
